properties.name: Key Route Pier
properties.geometry_method: Traced by eye from USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1915) (2 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol and fitted straight (RMS 3 m)); then traced by eye from USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1915) (4 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); the sheet corrected by a shift on 3 control points (Yerba Buena Island on the 1949 Oakland West sheet; +74 m E, +213 m N, RMS 44.8 m). The trestle runs straight from the shore, then curves to the ferry terminal.

sources.note: The sheet labels it "San Francisco–Oakland Terminal, Key Route Pier".
"A pier, over 3 miles in length, has been constructed from the Oakland shore" (p. 247); "the pier has a length of 16,240 ft." (p. 249).
"The first regular train service over the Key Route was inaugurated on Oct. 26" (1903).

"Prior to the opening of the … Bay Bridge to interurban rail traffic, Key System and Interurban's predecessor … provided passenger service across the Bay by ferry boat"; the bridge opened to rail service on January 15, 1939.

properties.notes: Ferry trains ran to its end until the Bay Bridge opened to trains in January 1939; from then its land end carried the bridge trains. A 1933 fire is relayed via Wikipedia only.

properties.name: Pier approach and subway to Poplar Junction
properties.geometry_method: Joined to key-pier at its start; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (3 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (4 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). From the pier's land end under the Southern Pacific main line (the 1903 subway) to Poplar Junction, along the line the 1949 sheet draws there.

sources.note: "In order to avoid a grade crossing with the Southern Pacific Company's main tracks at the land end of the pier" a subway; "The total length of the subway is 1070 ft".
"The last trains crossed the Bay Bridge in 1958."

properties.name: Yerba Buena Avenue to San Pablo Avenue
properties.geometry_method: Joined to key-trunk-shore at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (2 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol). Along Yerba Buena Avenue to the station at San Pablo Avenue.

sources.note: "For 2980 ft. east of the subway the double tracks are carried on Yerba Buena Avenue to the station at the crossing of San Pablo Avenue."
"The last trains crossed the Bay Bridge in 1958."

properties.name: East Bay yards to the old pier line
properties.geometry_method: Joined to bbr-east-approach at its end; then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (2 hand-read points, centred on the line symbol); then joined to key-pier at its start. From the East Bay yards over the bridge approach to the north side of the mole ("TRANSIT LINES" on the 1949 sheet), meeting the old pier line.

sources.note: "The last trains crossed the Bay Bridge in 1958."
Key lines ran "over joint track with the Interurban rail lines over the bridge to the East Bay Yards, thence proceeding over separate facilities from that point into the service area."

properties.name: Yerba Buena Avenue and 40th Street to Piedmont Avenue
properties.geometry_method: Joined to key-yerba-buena at its end; then along today's Yerba Buena Avenue centerline from -122.27980,37.82960 to 40th Street (260 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); then along today's 40th Street centerline from Yerba Buena Avenue to Piedmont Avenue (2134 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1, across gaps of up to 250 m where the street is cut today); checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949). Along Yerba Buena Avenue and 40th Street.

sources.note: "complete the Piedmont branch along Fortieth street"
"The terminal of the road will be on Piedmont avenue, between Fortieth and Forty-first streets." "Wednesday next at 10 a.m. the Key Route will inaugurate its ferry system in Piedmont."
Yerba Buena Avenue runs "from Adeline Street to 40th Street".
"The last trains crossed the Bay Bridge in 1958."

properties.name: San Pablo Avenue to Adeline Street, by Linden Street
properties.geometry_method: Joined to key-yerba-buena at its end; then along today's Linden Street centerline from -122.27900,37.83100 to -122.27530,37.83550 (509 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1, across gaps of up to 250 m where the street is cut today); then given point by point; checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949). "Nearly north" from San Pablo Avenue, crossing Temescal Creek on Linden Street; drawn along today's Linden Street and joined straight to Adeline Street, which the sources don't place exactly.

sources.note: "the Berkeley line branches off and runs nearly north"; "the Berkeley branch, which crosses Temescal Creek on Linden Street, on the short trestle".
"The last trains crossed the Bay Bridge in 1958."

properties.name: Adeline Street to Alcatraz Avenue
properties.geometry_method: Joined to key-linden-st at its end; then along today's Adeline Street centerline from -122.27450,37.83850 to Alcatraz Avenue (1194 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1, across gaps of up to 250 m where the street is cut today); checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949). Along Adeline Street to Alcatraz Avenue.

sources.note: "At its terminus in South Berkeley the Adeline Street line is situated parallel and immediately adjacent to the Shattuck Avenue line of Interurban on Adeline Street at Alcatraz Avenue."
"The last trains crossed the Bay Bridge in 1958."

properties.name: Adeline Street, Alcatraz Avenue to Shattuck Avenue (1903 track)
properties.geometry_method: Along today's Adeline Street centerline from Alcatraz Avenue to Shattuck Avenue (1289 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949). Beside the Southern Pacific's tracks on Adeline Street.

sources.note: "From Lorin station to Berkeley the Key Route parallels the Berkeley and Berryman local tracks of the Southern Pacific".

properties.name: Shattuck Avenue to Center Street
properties.geometry_method: Along today's Shattuck Avenue centerline from Adeline Street to Center Street (1182 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949). Beside the Southern Pacific's tracks on Shattuck Avenue.

sources.note: To "the business part of the city at Center Street and Shattuck Avenue".

properties.name: Adeline Street, Alcatraz Avenue to Shattuck Avenue (1941 track)
properties.geometry_method: Along today's Adeline Street centerline from Alcatraz Avenue to Shattuck Avenue (1289 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949). A single track built in 1941 beside the Interurban's, in the unpaved middle of Adeline Street.

sources.note: "construct a single track railway along Adeline Street between Alcatraz Avenue and Shattuck Avenue, a distance of approximately three quarters of one mile"; routes established July 26, 1941.
"constructing a single-track road immediately adjacent to and paralleling the rails of Interurban along the unpaved center section of the street".
"The last trains crossed the Bay Bridge in 1958."

properties.name: Poplar Junction to West Grand Avenue
properties.geometry_method: Joined to key-trunk-shore at its end; then given point by point; then along today's Poplar Street centerline from -122.28469,37.82298 to West Grand Avenue (774 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1). South from Poplar Junction on Poplar Street; the street's north end is gone today, so the first 700 m are joined straight.

sources.note: "Remaining portions of the \"A\" and \"B\" rail lines from Yerba Buena Avenue along Poplar Street and West Grand Avenue".
"the Twenty-second street Key Route line at Poplar Junction"
"The last trains crossed the Bay Bridge in 1958."

properties.name: 22nd Street (West Grand Avenue) to Broadway
properties.geometry_method: Along today's West Grand Avenue centerline from Poplar Street to Broadway (1882 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949). Along 22nd Street, today's West Grand Avenue, to Broadway.

sources.note: "The Twenty-Second Street or Oakland branch … was opened for regular traffic on May 16th." "The terminus of the new line is at Broadway and Twenty-Second Street".
"The last trains crossed the Bay Bridge in 1958."

properties.name: Poplar Street, West Grand Avenue to 12th Street
properties.geometry_method: Along today's Poplar Street centerline from West Grand Avenue to 12th Street (893 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1, across gaps of up to 250 m where the street is cut today); checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949). Along Poplar Street.

sources.note: "through train service was established yesterday"; "the last two cars taking the Poplar street route into Twelfth street and terminating for the present at Broadway".
"The last trains crossed the Bay Bridge in 1958."

properties.name: 12th Street to Broadway
properties.geometry_method: Along today's 12th Street centerline from Poplar Street to Broadway (1737 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1, across gaps of up to 250 m where the street is cut today); checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949). Along 12th Street to Broadway.

sources.note: The A line "continues along 12th Street through the downtown area of the City to the Bay Bridge".
"The last trains crossed the Bay Bridge in 1958."

properties.name: 12th Street, Broadway to Oak Street
properties.geometry_method: Along today's 12th Street centerline from Broadway to Oak Street (816 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949). Along 12th Street from Broadway to Oak Street.

sources.note: Terminus "12th and Oak Streets, Oakland (\"A\" Line)".
"The last trains crossed the Bay Bridge in 1958."

properties.name: Sacramento Street to Hopkins Street
properties.geometry_method: Along today's Sacramento Street centerline from Alcatraz Avenue to Hopkins Street (3710 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949). In the median of Sacramento Street.

sources.note: "The new Berkeley main line of the Key Route extends from Fifty-fourth and Adeline streets, Oakland, along Sacramento street to Hopkins street in Berkeley."
"Operation of the Sacramento street, Northbrae and Albany lines of the Key Route began this morning".
"Sacramento Street is divided into two driveways separated by the railroad right of way".
"the Sacramento Street line which was converted to motor coach operation on July 26, 1941".

properties.name: Hopkins Street to Northbrae (El Dorado Avenue)
properties.geometry_method: Along today's Hopkins Street centerline from Sacramento Street to -122.27420,37.88840 (1217 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); checked on USGS Richmond 1:24,000 (1949). Private right of way and Hopkins Street to El Dorado Avenue; drawn along today's Hopkins Street.

sources.note: "Along Hopkins street an extension runs through a private right of way to Northbrae".

Abandonment of the line "along private right of way and Hopkins Street between Rose Street Interlocking Tower (near the intersection of McGee Avenue and Hopkins Street) and the end of the line at El Dorado Avenue", authorized March 16, 1933.

properties.name: Ferry, Key Route pier to the Ferry Building
properties.geometry_method: The shortest path over today's water from -122.39341,37.79553 to -122.34754,37.81780 (4936 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1 land and water), kept off the shore: the sources give the terminals, not the course.

sources.note: "The first regular train service over the Key Route was inaugurated on Oct. 26" (1903): trains to the pier, and ferries on to San Francisco.
Train service over the bridge from January 15, 1939, replacing the ferries.
The San Francisco end: the Ferry Building's ferry terminal as 511's GTFS places it today.

properties.notes: The course isn't recorded: drawn as the shortest way over water between the terminals, round Yerba Buena Island.
